title: Station electrical and tower safety
blurb: Explain where fuses, GFCIs, interlocks and lightning grounds belong, and the precautions for towers, generators and solder.

G0B01.why: A fuse or breaker opens a **hot** wire. Fusing the neutral or ground could leave the circuit live or defeat the safety path.
G0B01.trap: Neutral and ground must stay unfused.

G0B02.why: A 20 A breaker needs wire rated for 20 A: **AWG 12**. Thinner wire (a higher AWG number) overheats.
G0B02.trap: Higher AWG numbers are thinner wire, not stronger.

G0B03.why: AWG 14 wire is rated for **15 A**. A larger breaker would let the wire overheat without tripping.

G0B04.why: A lightning ground goes **outside the building**, so the strike energy is dumped before it enters.

G0B05.why: A GFCI trips when current leaks **from a hot wire directly to ground**, for example through a person.
G0B05.trap: Hot to neutral is normal load current. A GFCI ignores it and overvoltage.

G0B06.why: The National Electrical Code covers **electrical safety of the station**: wiring, fusing and grounding. It doesn't cover RF or modulation.

G0B07.why: Check that the harness is **rated for the climber's weight** and **within its allowable service life**.

G0B08.why: Make sure **circuits that supply power to the tower are locked out and tagged** so nobody can re-energize them while you climb.
G0B08.trap: Ungrounding the tower makes it more dangerous.

G0B09.why: Exhaust contains carbon monoxide, so run the generator in a **well-ventilated area**.
G0B09.trap: Fuel stored near the generator is a fire hazard.

G0B10.why: Lead from solder reaches your mouth through food, so **wash your hands** carefully after handling it.

G0B11.why: Every lightning ground rod must be **bonded together with all other grounds**, so they rise and fall together.
G0B11.trap: The rule is to bond the grounds together. Ground wires should avoid sharp bends.

G0B12.why: An interlock cuts the AC feed when the cabinet opens, so **dangerous voltages are removed** before you can reach inside.
G0B12.trap: Thermal and overvoltage protection are different circuits.

G0B13.why: Place arrestors **where the feed lines enter the building**, diverting a surge to ground before it reaches the station.
